items_missed: Section 1 (Set Agenda): never asked her name (called her 'sir' the whole call — Cher never addressed by name), skipped 'how are you today,' never confirmed the move date was actually available on the calendar, no agenda statement laying out what the call would cover, no explicit 'sound good?' confirmation.

Section 2 (Probe): no stairs/floors question, no special considerations (hallways, turns, long carries), no box count, no storage question, no additional-stops question, no access/HOA/parking question, never asked if she had any worries about the move.

Section 3 (Pricing): skipped almost the entire section — no 'pricing is super simple' opener, no stated hourly rate per mover, no rundown of what's included (gas, truck, insurance, tools), no disassembly/reassembly mention, no explicit trip-fee explanation despite a 6-7hr out-of-town drive, no No Worries Damage Coverage, no Meet Your Mover, no On-Time Guarantee, no 'no hidden fees' pitch. Went straight from move details to a flat dollar range with none of the standard build-up.
Section 4 (Clock): clock policy never explained at all — no on-site start, no 2.5-hour minimum, no 15-min proration, no sense-check.

Section 5 (Estimate): referenced 'typical time ranges' but never gave an actual hours estimate, never stated crew size or number of trucks, no walk-distance note, no equivalents/analogy, no assembly/disassembly callout.

Section 6 (Save Your Ass): skipped entirely — no mention that prep shortens the move and lowers the bill, no consolidation examples, no 'take a carload' tip, even though she volunteered she's already boxing things herself, a perfect opening for this.

Section 7 (Quote/Booking): never attempted to lock in the date, never said no deposit is required, no email/confirmation mentioned at all, didn't ask 'any other questions before I let you go' — call just ended after hours were given.
Section 8 (Politeness): never used the customer's actual name (Cher) once in the entire call, relying only on 'sir.'
top_strength: The honest budget framing on the estimate was genuinely good: "I would rather give you a more conservative idea of a budget if you did want to use us rather than trying to sell you a dream with the bells and whistles and fail to deliver on that." He also handled the propane grill question with real confidence and specificity (tanks need to be empty, frame is fine) without missing a beat.
coaching_note: This call skipped almost the whole pricing and differentiators pitch — the single highest-value section on the scorecard — and jumped straight to a bottom-line number with no hourly rate, no 'what's included,' and none of our differentiators (No Worries coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee). Save Your Ass was a complete miss too, even though she told you outright she's already packing herself — that was a free opening to give the prep speech. Build the standard structure into every quote regardless of how casual or rambling the caller is: probe fully, walk the pricing story before the number, then close by attempting to book, stating no deposit is required, and confirming next steps by email. Also use the customer's name — you never called her by name once.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and patient with a rambling, hard-to-follow caller, with a couple of genuine warmth moments (reassuring her it's fine to call on a Sunday, thanking her for considering Einstein), but mostly transactional filler ('okay,' 'sounds good') and no name use or humor to push it higher.
